source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

china_plus_one.evidence: Company has been building capacities in a few more niche APIs as per the evolving demand scenario in the backdrop of 'China plus one' opportunities; management guided double-digit growth for FY26, with 'stronger momentum from China+1' cited as a key trigger alongside GLP-1 commercialisation.

rural.evidence: Rural demand was rising and continued to outpace urban sales growth, with rural sales accounting for roughly a third of Royal Enfield's sales in FY25 (two-wheeler segment; not full consolidated figure including VECV).

govt_capex.evidence: VECV's commercial vehicle business has revenue linkage to government infrastructure and construction activity, though no specific revenue percentage is disclosed in available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: Eicher Motors is among Champion OEM applicants that received DVA certification for EV variants under the Auto PLI scheme; potential incentive receipts estimated at INR 200-600 crore over the scheme duration, contingent on localization of powertrain, electronics and battery-pack components.

china_plus_one.evidence: ABB's strategy includes strengthening India as a manufacturing and export hub, with an ambition to make India its third-largest global market by revenue before 2030 (behind only the US and China); no explicit 'China+1' framing found in AR-derived text, but export/diversification momentum is emphasized.

govt_capex.evidence: ABB India remains a beneficiary of the government's capex investments in mega infrastructure and renewable projects, and converts business opportunities in industrial capex across metals & mining, energy & chemicals, and buildings/data centers.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company uses commodity and forex hedging; commodity hedging partly offset forex losses and higher metal (notably copper) input costs in recent quarters, per management commentary.
inr_exposure.evidence: 'The impact of new labour codes and forex loss in Q4 was largely offset by commodity hedging and efficiency gains.' Profitability faces near-term pressure from forex volatility, commodity price swings, and geopolitical uncertainty.

china_plus_one.evidence: 'With global companies derisking supply chains away from China, India is emerging as a strong alternative. Acutaas Chemicals is the first Indian company outside China to develop battery-grade electrolyte additives... Its acquisition of Baba Fine Chemicals for semiconductor chemicals enhances its leverage under the China+1 strategy.' Also: 'we have significantly reduced our dependence on Chinese imports, bringing China's share of raw material imports down from more than 70% to 21% by 2025, while increasing domestic and regional sourcing.'

rate_sensitive.evidence: Consolidated Notes to Financial Statements, Exposure to Interest Rate Risk (FY25): Borrowing bearing fixed rate of interest - Nil; Borrowing bearing variable rate of interest ₹818.43 Lakhs; Total ₹818.43 Lakhs — i.e., 100% of borrowings are floating-rate.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: The Company operates internationally with the major portion of business transacted in USD & EUR; foreign exchange exposure is partially balanced by natural hedge (purchasing goods/services in the same currencies) and derivatives such as foreign exchange forward and option contracts to hedge residual currency risk.
inr_exposure.evidence: 'The Company operates internationally and the major portion of business is transacted in USD & EURO... the company follows established risk management policies, including the use of derivatives like foreign exchange forward contracts to hedge exposure to foreign currency risk.' Unhedged exposure at FY25-end: USD ₹64.32 Lakhs and EUR ₹169.14 Lakhs (1% sensitivity impact on PBT).

china_plus_one.evidence: Despite headwinds, we are strategically positioned to seize global trends like China plus one strategy. The rising demand for refrigerant gases and agri-products...will drive growth in our HPP business. China+1 and Europe+1 strategy: Global companies are seeking to derisk and diversify their supply chain away from China. Key fluorospecialty consuming regions like USA, EU and Japan are considering India as their supply partner for reliable and timely supply of raw materials.

rate_sensitive.evidence: The Company/Group is mainly exposed to interest rate risk due to its variable interest rate borrowings. Borrowings bearing floating rate of interest: ₹1,339.94 crore (consolidated, FY24) vs ₹848.65 crore (FY23); no fixed-rate borrowings category disclosed separately.

crude_exposure.evidence: Raw material costs, accounting for a 45% share of the Company's revenues, increased by 4% from ₹896 crores in FY 2022-23 to ₹935 crores in FY 2023-24 due to the change in business mix and decline in prices of refrigerant gases.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Board approved Foreign Currency Risk Management Policy; hedges foreign exchange risk using foreign exchange forward contracts; policy is to selectively hedge net transaction exposures in major foreign currencies.
inr_exposure.evidence: Any risk arising from exposure to foreign currency for exports and imports is being hedged on a continuous basis.

pli_scheme.evidence: Moreover, the Government of India's PLI scheme for API manufacturing in the pharmaceutical and specialty chemical sectors is a significant driving force behind the growth of the fluorospecialty market (industry-level commentary; no company-specific PLI participation confirmed in the AR).

crude_exposure.evidence: The Company is exposed to fluctuations in gold price (including fluctuations in foreign currency) arising on purchase/sale of gold. To manage the variability, the Company enters into derivative financial instruments...primarily in the nature of future commodity contracts and forward foreign exchange contracts. The risk management strategy against gold price fluctuation also includes procuring gold on loan basis, with a flexibility to fix price of gold at any time during the tenor of the loan.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Hedges gold price and foreign currency risk via future commodity contracts and forward foreign exchange contracts; also uses Gold on Lease/gold-on-loan procurement and designates fair-value/cash-flow hedges for gold price movements.
inr_exposure.evidence: The Company designates derivative contracts as hedging instruments to mitigate the risk of change in fair value of hedged item due to movement in gold prices.

govt_capex.evidence: Government (central and state) orders contribute ~52% of the current orderbook, plus 8% from Government-owned enterprises (PSUs), as of March 2025 — i.e. ~60% of ORDER BOOK (not revenue) is government-linked; private sector is the remaining ~40% of order book.

rate_sensitive.evidence: The Group's exposure to the risk of changes in market interest rates relates primarily to the Group's total debt obligations with floating interest rates.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Overseas project risk mitigated via forward contracts and currency options, alongside political risk insurance and diversification.
inr_exposure.evidence: A clear understanding of the overseas market, forward contracts and currency options, political risk insurance, diversification and use of technology [cited as mitigants for overseas market/political-instability risk].

china_plus_one.evidence: As global supply chains continue to diversify, our strong alignment with India's industrial growth becomes increasingly evident. ... Amid geopolitical instability and global trade restrictions...the Company swiftly activated contingency plans...It diversified sourcing and logistics strategies, established alternative shipping routes.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Variable rate borrowings 134.63; Fixed rate borrowings – nil; Total borrowings 134.63 (as at 31st March 2025, standalone, INR crore).

crude_exposure.evidence: Material Cost 15,447 (INR million), 43% of Total Income in FY 2024-25 (43% in FY 2023-24 also). Cost of materials consumed primarily includes special steel alloy bars, iron castings, steel blanks and bolts...

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Board approved hedging policy which primarily employs forward contracts as a medium of hedging currency risk.
inr_exposure.evidence: Your Company operates internationally, and a large portion of the business is transacted in international currencies primarily in US$ and EUR. Consequently, we are exposed to foreign exchange risk through our sales and services in the USA, Europe, China and other countries...

pli_scheme.evidence: We benefited from income accrual from the Auto PLI scheme, for which we had eight products approved...It achieved this by advancing product development and securing Production Linked Incentive (PLI) certifications for its electric two-wheeler portfolio.

china_plus_one.evidence: Emcure continues to demonstrate strong geographical diversification, with sales spanning over 70 countries; international revenue rose 20.5% YoY to 54% of total sales, driven by growth in Canada and Emerging Markets, with Europe showing early traction through product approvals and portfolio acquisitions supporting future expansion.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Natural hedge: offsets foreign currency payables (trade obligations, loans) against foreign currency receivables; monitors currency positions and may use financial instruments for residual risk
inr_exposure.evidence: Emcure offsets foreign currency payables—such as trade obligations and loans—against foreign currency receivables, creating a natural hedge.

pli_scheme.evidence: Emcure Pharma was among domestic pharmaceutical companies (alongside Biocon, MSN Labs, Wockhardt, Alembic, Macleods, Biological E, Natco, Strides) approved in Group B of the PLI scheme for APIs/KSMs/Drug Intermediates.

rural.evidence: Nestlé India's 'RUrban' rural-urban distribution model has expanded to 28,240 touchpoints since 2019, reaching ~209,050 villages; older (2021) estimates put rural contribution at 20-25% of sales, but this does not correspond to the current report year and was not re-disclosed in the FY24-25 AR per available sources.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Nestlé India holds a net cash position (~₹3.66B cash vs ~₹714M debt as of Sep 2025); interest coverage ~29.1x EBIT, implying minimal floating-rate debt exposure, though no specific % was disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Management commentary notes milk, green coffee, wheat and fuel inflation remain elevated while crude and edible oil prices have started cooling off; gross margin contracted ~250bps YoY to 55.2% due to high commodity prices.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports represented approximately 4.6% of Nestlé India's total sales (₹290.22 crore of ₹6,363.27 crore in a recent quarter); the company was awarded 4-Star Export House status and expanded MAGGI/NESCAFÉ presence in Canada, Europe, UAE, Saudi Arabia and Lebanon.

pli_scheme.evidence: Nestlé India Limited received government approval (December 2021) under the Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Food Processing Industry (PLISFPI) for the processed fruits & vegetables category.

china_plus_one.evidence: Global Specialty vertical contributed ~20% of FY25 consolidated revenue, with specialty sales up 24.8% YoY driven by ILUMYA, CEQUA, ODOMZO and WINLEVI; Emerging Markets grew 7% to $1.114bn and Rest of World grew 4.5% to $847m. No explicit China+1/supply-chain-diversification framing tied to revenue growth was found in available sources.

inr_exposure.evidence: Sun Pharma holds foreign currency-denominated debt and incurs operating expenses abroad, making it vulnerable to USD/INR and JPY/INR exchange rate fluctuations; the U.S. contributes approximately 30-35% of revenue and Japan around 5-10%.

pli_scheme.evidence: Sun Pharma is referenced generally among large pharma companies operating within India's PLI ecosystem, but no company-specific confirmation of PLI beneficiary status, incentive amount, or revenue impact was found in available sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: Lupin's API and CDMO businesses reflected strong alignment with global industry trends such as supply chain diversification, CDMO outsourcing, and high-potency APIs, as global pharma companies diversify away from China (India's CDMO market projected to grow from USD 3.5bn to USD 25bn over the next decade); FY25 was described as a transformational year for Lupin Manufacturing Solutions (CDMO).

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Natural hedges and forex derivatives deployed; treasury operations actively monitor exposures and adopt layered hedging strategies within a 'three lines of defense' risk governance framework
inr_exposure.evidence: Operating in 100+ markets exposes Lupin to currency fluctuations, particularly USD-INR, EUR-INR, and ZAR-INR.

pli_scheme.evidence: Lupin Limited is listed as a major beneficiary of the PLI scheme, investing in domestic production of APIs, bulk drugs, and complex generics.

china_plus_one.evidence: Bharat Forge is expanding capacity at its US and Europe sites to serve OEMs locally and capture share amid China+1 supply-chain shifts; aerospace exports have scaled 4x in five years to ~15% of industrial exports (analyst/IR commentary, not a direct AR quote).

govt_capex.evidence: Bharat Forge group secured new orders worth Rs 6,959 crore in FY25 with Defence accounting for 70% of those orders; defence order book provides ~3 years of revenue visibility at current run-rates.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw material is steel/alloy inputs for forging, not crude-linked; no direct crude-oil cost exposure disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Reported to actively hedge a portion of anticipated FX exposure (analyst estimate ~45% of exposure in 2024); no precise AR-disclosed hedge ratio confirmed.
inr_exposure.evidence: ~30% of consolidated revenue from exports; a 10% INR depreciation was noted to raise import costs of technology/inputs, offsetting some export competitiveness gains.

pli_scheme.evidence: Bharat Forge is among the companies approved under the Component Champion category of the Auto PLI scheme.

rural.evidence: Rural markets flagged as a growing area of strategic importance going forward, though FY25 rural-urban revenue split was not disclosed in available sources; Prestige & Above segment reached 89.2% of net sales in Q3 FY25, reflecting continued premiumisation.

china_plus_one.evidence: Direct exports currently account for only 3-4% of Gabriel India's portfolio; management plans to raise this to ~10% over time, supported by solar dampers, e-bike suspension products and deeper ties with global OEMs, but no explicit China+1/supply-chain-diversification framing was found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Total raw material cost (steel, rubber/elastomer and other inputs) was reported at roughly 74.8%-75.3% of sales in recent quarters; no separate crude-oil-linked cost breakdown was disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Direct exports account for only 3-4% of revenue; geographic export mix cited as Asia 28%, Americas 28%, Europe 27%, Africa 14%, Australia 4% (from a recent investor presentation).

rural.evidence: Consumers in states such as Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra are increasingly shifting to white spirits; vodka's share of alcohol consumption in Uttar Pradesh rose from ~10.4% in FY24 to nearly 17% in FY25, indicating rural/semi-urban demand momentum.

inr_exposure.evidence: In FY25, Radico's export segment contributed approximately 8-9% of revenue and 4-5% of volume, with a footprint in 100+ countries across six continents; a new 50% US tariff on Indian goods was noted as a headwind for export brands like Rampur Jugalbandi.

rural.evidence: Management commentary (FY25 quarterly calls) referenced 'healthy rural traction' in some quarters and rural/semi-urban demand remaining under strain in others; no annual-report percentage disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: VAM (vinyl acetate monomer), a crude oil derivative, accounts for approximately 35-40% of Pidilite's raw material costs; company has flagged crude-linked input cost inflation (geopolitical tensions in West Asia) as a margin risk.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Bosch Ltd is a largely cash-rich, low-debt company; no material floating-rate liability disclosed in available sources.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports at ~INR 14,054 million constitute approximately 8.3% of total sales in FY2024-25; bulk of exports are manufactured goods to other Bosch group companies, with close to 69% of total exports going to Robert Bosch, Germany.

pli_scheme.evidence: Management stated one of their plants does not qualify under PLI and they did not apply, though they continue screening PLI schemes (per earnings call commentary).

china_plus_one.evidence: Industry/analyst commentary on Sai Life: 'The China+1 supply chain strategy — where Western pharma companies deliberately diversify away from China-only sourcing — is creating a multi-year demand wave for Indian CRDMOs... Sai Life Sciences is directly positioned to capture that wave, with 280+ global clients already embedded in its programs.' Note: sourced from secondary market commentary, not a direct AR quote (primary AR PDF was not accessible).

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports account for approximately 99% of total revenues, primarily from the US and Europe (FY24 disclosure); detailed geographic revenue split (US vs Europe) not separately disclosed per analyst commentary noting management does not provide granular geographic breakdowns.

china_plus_one.evidence: CDMO segment (~11% of FY25 revenue) and international formulations exports exist and grew (~10.6% international growth in FY25, driven by South Africa, Russia-CIS, and US), but no explicit company-attributed China+1/diversification narrative was found (only generic industry commentary that India is a preferred CDMO destination amid China+1 trends).

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company adopted a conservative approach to protect the bottom line in view of political developments in Russia/Ukraine and sharp depreciation of the Russian ruble against the US dollar.
inr_exposure.evidence: JB Chemicals recorded a mark-to-market (MTM) forex impact of INR 4 crores due to ruble depreciation; exports for Russia-CIS region amounted to ~INR 69.26 crores (lower YoY as sales shifted through a wholly-owned Dubai subsidiary).
